- builder: Mid-tier implementer for well-scoped changes with a clear spec: apply a planned edit, write a test from a described behavior, mechanical refactors, doc/report updates. Give it exact files and acceptance criteria. Not for open-ended design or ambiguous debugging - keep those in the orchestrator session.
 (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Edit, Write, Bash)
- claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- nori-change-documenter: Creates documentation about changes to a codebase. Call the nori-change-documenter whenever you change the codebase. Provide all of the relevance context for *why* the change was made. Be extremely detailed! Provide as much context as possible so the agent can accurately update documentation. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, LS, Write, Edit, Bash)

- nori-codebase-analyzer: Analyzes codebase implementation details. Call the nori-codebase-analyzer agent when you need to find detailed information about specific components. As always, the more detailed your request prompt, the better! :) (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, LS)

- nori-codebase-locator: Locates files, directories, and components relevant to a feature or task. Call `nori-codebase-locator` with human language prompt describing what you're looking for. Basically a "Super Grep/Glob/LS tool" — Use it if you find yourself desiring to use one of these tools more than once. (Tools: Grep, Glob, LS)

- nori-codebase-pattern-finder: nori-codebase-pattern-finder is a useful subagent_type for finding similar implementations, usage examples, or existing patterns that can be modeled after. It will give you concrete code examples based on what you're looking for! It's sorta like nori-codebase-locator, but it will not only tell you the location of files, it will also give you code details! (Tools: Grep, Glob, Read, LS)

- nori-initial-documenter: Creates documentation about a codebase. This agent creates the initial documentation for the codebase; use this agent when you want to create documentation and no existing documentation is present. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, LS, Write, Edit, Bash)

- nori-web-search-researcher: Do you find yourself desiring information that you don't quite feel well-trained (confident) on? Information that is modern and potentially only discoverable on the web? Use the nori-web-search-researcher subagent_type today to find any and all answers to your questions! It will research deeply to figure out and attempt to answer your questions! If you aren't immediately satisfied you can get your money back! (Not really - but you can re-run nori-web-search-researcher with an altered prompt in the event you're not satisfied the first time) (Tools: WebSearch, WebFetch, TodoWrite, Read, Grep, Glob, LS)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- reviewer: High-judgment read-only review. Use to check a diff or design for correctness bugs, edge cases, and simpler alternatives before integrating - especially work produced by builder agents. Returns findings with file:line references and severity; does not fix anything.
 (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash)

- scout: Cheap, fast read-only recon, executed on GPT-5.6 Terra (medium reasoning) via the Codex CLI. Use for searches, file inventories, "where is X defined/used", summarizing a file or directory, running read-only bd/git commands or tests and reporting output verbatim. No editing. Delegate here whenever the task is mechanical lookup rather than judgment. Prefer calling `scripts/codex-agent scout` directly from the orchestrator when you can (same isolation, no relay hop; include the recon rules from this file in the prompt); this agent type is the interface for workflow agentType calls and the fallback when codex is unavailable.
 (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

427	The verifier runs locally, without GitHub Actions or status polling:
428	
429	```bash
430	scripts/verify-status
431	scripts/verify-next          # runs one queued job
432	```
433	
434	On Linux the queue self-drains: the `verify-babysit` systemd user timer
435	(installed via `scripts/install-verify-babysit`, fires every 15 min, zero
436	model tokens) runs `verify-next` once per fire. The oneshot unit will not
437	start while a previous run is still going, so long suites serialize
438	naturally; the unit's `VERIFY_TIMEOUT=100m` covers suite commands that carry
439	their own 90m timeouts. Do not also run `verify-next` manually while the
440	timer is installed unless you are debugging a specific failure.
441	
442	From PowerShell on Windows, invoke these via Git Bash as shown in the Windows
443	housekeeping section.
444	
445	`verify-next` creates a clean detached worktree under
446	`<mybd-root>/.worktrees/beads/verify-*`, runs the recorded
447	`verify_cmd`, stores logs under `.worktrees/beads/.verify-logs/`, and writes
448	`verify_state=passed|failed` plus result metadata back to bd. Keep full-suite
449	concurrency low by default; Beads/Dolt tests are process and disk heavy.

- quota-watch: Monitor Amp Free quota and handoff before exhaustion. Use when user says quota-watch, check quota, or monitor usage.
- initialize-noridocs: Initialize docs.md files throughout the codebase
- nori-create-skillset: Create a new custom skillset by cloning an existing skillset
- nori-switch-skillset: Switch between Nori configuration skillsets (amol, senior-swe, product-manager, documenter, none)
- session-close: Cold-start-readiness check before ending a work session - runs the 3 judgment prompts plus the mechanical backstop, then the standard close/push.
- setup-beads-sync: Set up a private GitHub Dolt repo for personal beads and configure sync for the current project
- switch-nori-profile: Switch between Nori configuration profiles (amol, senior-swe, product-manager, documenter, none)
- triage: Layer 2 issue triage - mirror upstream into bd, classify each stub to a one-line disposition, emit a short digest. Never posts text upstream.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, keeping state shared across viewers, or updating and republishing itself. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

1	# Maintainer PR Guidelines
2	
3	This is the source of truth for agents triaging, reviewing, landing, closing, or otherwise maintaining pull requests for `mybd` and upstream beads work.
4	
5	## Philosophy
6	
7	Help contributors get to the finish line. Optimize for community throughput.
8	
9	For every PR, look for the value in it and choose the action that moves useful work into the codebase with the least contributor starvation. If a PR contains something worth keeping, absorb that value directly when practical: accept it as-is, fix bugs, improve the architecture, rename things, turn it into a plugin, cherry-pick parts, or reject the parts that do not fit.
10	
11	The goal is not to block contributors unnecessarily. The goal is to identify useful work, preserve it, and keep the project moving.
12	
13	For upstream beads PRs that change product surface area, read
14	[bd-main/docs/PROJECT_CHARTER.md](bd-main/docs/PROJECT_CHARTER.md). Scope
15	boundaries should guide where value lands: core, metadata, integration, plugin,
16	orchestration layer, or external tool.
17	
18	## Contributor Protection
19	
20	External contributor PRs have priority. Before implementing related work, opening a competing PR, or closing a PR, check whether an existing contributor PR already addresses the same area.
21	
22	- Review contributor work first. Read the PR description, changed files, linked issues, tests, CI status, and latest discussion.
23	- Build on the contributor branch by default. If the PR branch allows maintainer edits, push maintainer fix commits directly to that branch instead of opening a replacement PR.
24	- Preserve contributor tests unless they are actually wrong.
25	- Preserve attribution with original commits when possible. Maintainer commits on a contributor branch should keep the contributor's original commits intact; transformed local commits must use `Co-authored-by:` and PR references.
26	- Never close, supersede, or replace a contributor PR silently. Explain what was preserved, what changed, and why.
27	- Open a replacement PR only when in-place maintainer edits are not possible or would create a larger risk, such as when the contributor branch is not writable, the branch history is unusable, or the accepted change must be substantially reimplemented. Document that reason in both PR threads.
28	- If a rewrite is unavoidable, credit the contributor's design, tests, bug report, or use case in the replacement commit or PR.
29	
30	## How a Review Opens and Closes
31	
32	The rules above protect the contributor's *code*. These protect the reason they
33	came back. They are cheap, they cost no rigor, and they are the part that drifts
34	silently because nothing fails when they are skipped.
35	
36	Measured 2026-07-25 over the previous six weeks (19 changes-requested + 20
37	approving reviews on outside-contributor PRs), against steveyegge's first eleven
38	weeks of maintainership (117 contributor-facing messages):
39	
40	| | thanks the contributor when asking for changes | when approving |
41	|---|---|---|
42	| steveyegge, Oct–Dec 2025 | 66% | 26% |
43	| here, Jun–Jul 2026 | **5%** | 65% |
44	
45	A near-perfect inversion. Warmth on approval rewards compliance; warmth on
46	refusal is what makes someone try again. Concretely:
47	
48	- **The first sentence belongs to the contributor, not to us.** All 19
49	  changes-requested reviews in that sample opened with the identical string
50	  `Cross-vendor agent review (Codex … primary trace; Claude adjudication …)`.
51	  Review provenance is real and worth recording — put it at the **bottom**, next
52	  to the `Agent-Signature` line. Open on the specific thing their patch got
53	  right, named precisely enough that they can tell it was read.
54	- **Thank them in the changes-requested review, not only in the approval.** Zero
55	  of 19 did; 13 of 20 approvals did.
56	- **Say what the review volume means.** A 400-word audit reads as being audited
57	  unless told otherwise. One clause fixes it: *"docs that match the binary are
58	  worth this much scrutiny"* (gastownhall/beads#4913).
59	- **`CHANGES_REQUESTED` is not a notepad.** The Outcomes list already calls
60	  request-changes a last resort that can strand contributor work; it then became
61	  the default opening 19 times in six weeks, 7 of which we fixed ourselves
62	  anyway. A `COMMENT` review carries identical findings without stamping a red ✗
63	  on someone's first contribution.
64	- **Ask before finishing their PR for them.** Absorbing is correct policy, but
65	  "the fixes are applied as maintainer commits" as the contributor's *next news*
66	  removes the thing they came for. Offer first: *"Want to take these, or shall
67	  I push them?"*
68	- **Do not post the disposition and close in the same second.** All five sampled
69	  2026 declines closed 0–1s after the comment; none of 17 contributors replied
70	  to any of them, even though every message thanked them, preserved attribution
71	  and offered a route back. The generosity lands in a locked room. Contrast
72	  gastownhall/beads#77 (2025-10-18): the decline sat open for eight hours, the
73	  contributor replied, and *they* asked for the close. Leave the PR open at
74	  least 48h after a disposition comment, or hand the close to the patrol.
75	
76	None of this softens a finding. State the blocker exactly as harshly as the
77	evidence warrants — just do not make the apparatus the first thing they meet.
78	
79	**Do not automate the greeting.** A patrol *could* post "thanks, this is in the
80	review queue" on unanswered contributor PRs, and it would silence the polite
81	pings at zero token cost. Owner decision, maphew 2026-07-25: **no** — an
82	essentially empty bot auto-response is worse than silence, because it converts an
83	honest "nobody has looked at this yet" into a false signal that someone has. The
84	fix for a contributor waiting is a human answer sooner (see mybd-aayb), not a
85	faster acknowledgement of the wait. The patrol may automate the *close* of a
86	disposition already written by an agent (mybd-sx1w); it may not originate
87	contributor-facing text.
88	
89	## Triage Groups
90	
91	Classify each PR into one of these groups:
92	
93	- **Easy win**: Targeted bug fixes, documentation updates, dependency bot upgrades, drafts to close, PRs from banned contributors, and other low-risk cases.
94	- **Fix-merge candidate**: A PR that otherwise fits easy-win criteria but has a simple blocker, such as failed CI, a needed rebase, or a small implementation error.
95	- **Needs review**: A PR that looks suspicious, complex, broad, risky, or otherwise requires deeper investigation.
96	
97	Easy wins can be handled automatically during a PR review run and by recurring patrols. Fix-merge candidates can also be handled automatically when the maintainer determines the repair is simple enough to make locally.
98	
99	Needs-review PRs require a deeper agent review and a concrete report. The maintainer can summarize those reports or inspect the agent sessions directly.
100	
101	### Sweep by author, not by age
102	
103	When working the open-PR queue, prefer **author-clustered sweeps**: pick one contributor, process all of their open PRs in a single session, and leave them a single consolidated picture (what merged, what was fixed on their branches, what needs their judgment, what was retired and why).
104	
105	Why this beats oldest-first or one-at-a-time:
106	
107	- One context load covers the author's style, recurring themes, and cross-PR dependencies — their PRs often share branches-behind-main problems, overlapping files, or one design thread.
108	- The contributor gets one coherent conversation instead of scattered verdicts, and follow-ups concentrate into one tracking bead (e.g. mybd-5bz2).
109	- Retirements land better when paired with merges of the same author's other work — attribution and goodwill are preserved in context.
110	- It converts the queue into a finite list of named clusters, which makes progress visible and delegable (one sweep bead per author).
111	
112	Reference runs: `reports/2026-07-23-coffeegoddd-pr-sweep.md` (6 PRs: 2 merged with maintainer fixes, 3 retired with re-cut requirements, follow-ups in one bead) and the johnzook triage (`reports/johnzook-pr-triage-2026-07-03.md`). Pick the next cluster by open-PR count and staleness (`gh pr list --repo gastownhall/beads --state open --json author | jq ...`).
113	
114	## Outcomes
115	
116	Use these recommendations after review:
117	
118	- **Easy win**: The PR turns out to fit easy-win criteria after all.
119	- **Merge**: Recommend merge. The PR is well-tested, broadly useful, well-documented, and ready as-is.
120	- **Merge-fix**: Merge the PR as-is, then push a follow-up fix to `main`. Use when the remaining issues are safe to repair afterward.
121	- **Fix-merge**: Pull the PR locally, make substantial fixes on the contributor branch, then push the branch so the original PR can merge. Use when the PR is busted but valuable and maintainer edits are possible.
122	- **Cherry-pick**: Keep only selected items from a PR with multiple features or fixes. Commit the useful parts locally with attribution, then close the PR with an explanation.
123	- **Split-merge**: Split a multi-concern PR into separate commits, then push all accepted parts with attribution to the original contributor.
124	- **Replacement PR**: Carry useful work into a new maintainer PR only after confirming the original branch cannot reasonably be fixed in place. Preserve attribution with original commits where possible, otherwise use `Co-authored-by:` trailers and PR references, and explain the reason replacement was necessary.
125	- **Redesign/reimplement**: Reject the submitted design but solve the underlying problem another way. Close the PR with thanks and an explanation.
126	- **Retire**: Close an obsolete PR with thanks because it was superseded or already fixed elsewhere.
127	- **Reject**: Close politely when the feature does not pay its weight in tech debt, is too niche for core, or the design does not meet project standards.
128	- **Request changes**: Last resort. Avoid this when the maintainer or agents can reasonably absorb, transform, or land the useful parts directly.
129

# Maintainer PR Guidelines

This is the source of truth for agents triaging, reviewing, landing, closing, or otherwise maintaining pull requests for `mybd` and upstream beads work.

## Philosophy

Help contributors get to the finish line. Optimize for community throughput.

For every PR, look for the value in it and choose the action that moves useful work into the codebase with the least contributor starvation. If a PR contains something worth keeping, absorb that value directly when practical: accept it as-is, fix bugs, improve the architecture, rename things, turn it into a plugin, cherry-pick parts, or reject the parts that do not fit.

The goal is not to block contributors unnecessarily. The goal is to identify useful work, preserve it, and keep the project moving.

For upstream beads PRs that change product surface area, read
[bd-main/docs/PROJECT_CHARTER.md](bd-main/docs/PROJECT_CHARTER.md). Scope
boundaries should guide where value lands: core, metadata, integration, plugin,
orchestration layer, or external tool.

## Contributor Protection

External contributor PRs have priority. Before implementing related work, opening a competing PR, or closing a PR, check whether an existing contributor PR already addresses the same area.

- Review contributor work first. Read the PR description, changed files, linked issues, tests, CI status, and latest discussion.
- Build on the contributor branch by default. If the PR branch allows maintainer edits, push maintainer fix commits directly to that branch instead of opening a replacement PR.
- Preserve contributor tests unless they are actually wrong.
- Preserve attribution with original commits when possible. Maintainer commits on a contributor branch should keep the contributor's original commits intact; transformed local commits must use `Co-authored-by:` and PR references.
- Never close, supersede, or replace a contributor PR silently. Explain what was preserved, what changed, and why.
- Open a replacement PR only when in-place maintainer edits are not possible or would create a larger risk, such as when the contributor branch is not writable, the branch history is unusable, or the accepted change must be substantially reimplemented. Document that reason in both PR threads.
- If a rewrite is unavoidable, credit the contributor's design, tests, bug report, or use case in the replacement commit or PR.

## How a Review Opens and Closes

The rules above protect the contributor's *code*. These protect the reason they
came back. They are cheap, they cost no rigor, and they are the part that drifts
silently because nothing fails when they are skipped.

Measured 2026-07-25 over the previous six weeks (19 changes-requested + 20
approving reviews on outside-contributor PRs), against steveyegge's first eleven
weeks of maintainership (117 contributor-facing messages):

| | thanks the contributor when asking for changes | when approving |
|---|---|---|
| steveyegge, Oct–Dec 2025 | 66% | 26% |
| here, Jun–Jul 2026 | **5%** | 65% |

A near-perfect inversion. Warmth on approval rewards compliance; warmth on
refusal is what makes someone try again. Concretely:

- **The first sentence belongs to the contributor, not to us.** All 19
  changes-requested reviews in that sample opened with the identical string
  `Cross-vendor agent review (Codex … primary trace; Claude adjudication …)`.
  Review provenance is real and worth recording — put it at the **bottom**, next
  to the `Agent-Signature` line. Open on the specific thing their patch got
  right, named precisely enough that they can tell it was read.
- **Thank them in the changes-requested review, not only in the approval.** Zero
  of 19 did; 13 of 20 approvals did.
- **Say what the review volume means.** A 400-word audit reads as being audited
  unless told otherwise. One clause fixes it: *"docs that match the binary are
  worth this much scrutiny"* (gastownhall/beads#4913).
- **`CHANGES_REQUESTED` is not a notepad.** The Outcomes list already calls
  request-changes a last resort that can strand contributor work; it then became
  the default opening 19 times in six weeks, 7 of which we fixed ourselves
  anyway. A `COMMENT` review carries identical findings without stamping a red ✗
  on someone's first contribution.
- **Ask before finishing their PR for them.** Absorbing is correct policy, but
  "the fixes are applied as maintainer commits" as the contributor's *next news*
  removes the thing they came for. Offer first: *"Want to take these, or shall
  I push them?"*
- **Do not post the disposition and close in the same second.** All five sampled
  2026 declines closed 0–1s after the comment; none of 17 contributors replied
  to any of them, even though every message thanked them, preserved attribution
  and offered a route back. The generosity lands in a locked room. Contrast
  gastownhall/beads#77 (2025-10-18): the decline sat open for eight hours, the
  contributor replied, and *they* asked for the close. Leave the PR open at
  least 48h after a disposition comment, or hand the close to the patrol.

None of this softens a finding. State the blocker exactly as harshly as the
evidence warrants — just do not make the apparatus the first thing they meet.

**Do not automate the greeting.** A patrol *could* post "thanks, this is in the
review queue" on unanswered contributor PRs, and it would silence the polite
pings at zero token cost. Owner decision, maphew 2026-07-25: **no** — an
essentially empty bot auto-response is worse than silence, because it converts an
honest "nobody has looked at this yet" into a false signal that someone has. The
fix for a contributor waiting is a human answer sooner (see mybd-aayb), not a
faster acknowledgement of the wait. The patrol may automate the *close* of a
disposition already written by an agent (mybd-sx1w); it may not originate
contributor-facing text.

## Triage Groups

Classify each PR into one of these groups:

- **Easy win**: Targeted bug fixes, documentation updates, dependency bot upgrades, drafts to close, PRs from banned contributors, and other low-risk cases.
- **Fix-merge candidate**: A PR that otherwise fits easy-win criteria but has a simple blocker, such as failed CI, a needed rebase, or a small implementation error.
- **Needs review**: A PR that looks suspicious, complex, broad, risky, or otherwise requires deeper investigation.

Easy wins can be handled automatically during a PR review run and by recurring patrols. Fix-merge candidates can also be handled automatically when the maintainer determines the repair is simple enough to make locally.

Needs-review PRs require a deeper agent review and a concrete report. The maintainer can summarize those reports or inspect the agent sessions directly.

### Sweep by author, not by age

When working the open-PR queue, prefer **author-clustered sweeps**: pick one contributor, process all of their open PRs in a single session, and leave them a single consolidated picture (what merged, what was fixed on their branches, what needs their judgment, what was retired and why).

Why this beats oldest-first or one-at-a-time:

- One context load covers the author's style, recurring themes, and cross-PR dependencies — their PRs often share branches-behind-main problems, overlapping files, or one design thread.
- The contributor gets one coherent conversation instead of scattered verdicts, and follow-ups concentrate into one tracking bead (e.g. mybd-5bz2).
- Retirements land better when paired with merges of the same author's other work — attribution and goodwill are preserved in context.
- It converts the queue into a finite list of named clusters, which makes progress visible and delegable (one sweep bead per author).

Reference runs: `reports/2026-07-23-coffeegoddd-pr-sweep.md` (6 PRs: 2 merged with maintainer fixes, 3 retired with re-cut requirements, follow-ups in one bead) and the johnzook triage (`reports/johnzook-pr-triage-2026-07-03.md`). Pick the next cluster by open-PR count and staleness (`gh pr list --repo gastownhall/beads --state open --json author | jq ...`).

## Outcomes

Use these recommendations after review:

- **Easy win**: The PR turns out to fit easy-win criteria after all.
- **Merge**: Recommend merge. The PR is well-tested, broadly useful, well-documented, and ready as-is.
- **Merge-fix**: Merge the PR as-is, then push a follow-up fix to `main`. Use when the remaining issues are safe to repair afterward.
- **Fix-merge**: Pull the PR locally, make substantial fixes on the contributor branch, then push the branch so the original PR can merge. Use when the PR is busted but valuable and maintainer edits are possible.
- **Cherry-pick**: Keep only selected items from a PR with multiple features or fixes. Commit the useful parts locally with attribution, then close the PR with an explanation.
- **Split-merge**: Split a multi-concern PR into separate commits, then push all accepted parts with attribution to the original contributor.
- **Replacement PR**: Carry useful work into a new maintainer PR only after confirming the original branch cannot reasonably be fixed in place. Preserve attribution with original commits where possible, otherwise use `Co-authored-by:` trailers and PR references, and explain the reason replacement was necessary.
- **Redesign/reimplement**: Reject the submitted design but solve the underlying problem another way. Close the PR with thanks and an explanation.
- **Retire**: Close an obsolete PR with thanks because it was superseded or already fixed elsewhere.
- **Reject**: Close politely when the feature does not pay its weight in tech debt, is too niche for core, or the design does not meet project standards.
- **Request changes**: Last resort. Avoid this when the maintainer or agents can reasonably absorb, transform, or land the useful parts directly.

Other outcomes are possible, including rerouting a PR to the right project or banning a contributor, but the list above covers the normal cases.

## Operating Rules

- Prefer landing or transforming useful work over asking the contributor to do more rounds.
- Preserve contributor attribution when absorbing, fixing, cherry-picking, splitting, or reimplementing PR value.
- Before opening a competing or replacement PR, attempt the contributor-branch path first: fetch the PR, test it, make maintainer fix commits on that branch when permitted, and push back to the same PR.
- Be explicit when closing a PR: thank the contributor, state the outcome, and explain what was accepted, rejected, superseded, or implemented differently. Then leave the PR open — see "How a Review Opens and Closes" for why the close is a separate act from the disposition comment.
- Consider the entire PR thread. Valuable clarifying info are often in the comments.
- Treat request-changes as exceptional because it can strand contributor work.
- File follow-up work as beads issues instead of hidden notes.
- When code changes result from PR maintenance, follow repo quality gates and session completion rules in `AGENTS.md`.
- Post multi-line PR comments from a real Markdown body file or a shell heredoc, not from strings with escaped `\n` sequences. After posting or editing, verify the rendered body with `gh pr view --comments --json comments --jq ...` before moving on.
- Before finishing, re-read the PR, latest comments, review threads, and linked issues; address or explicitly note any unresolved action items.

## Base-Branch Health (stop-the-line)

When upstream main is red, per-PR check verdicts stop being reliable: every PR
inherits red checks, and "these failures are pre-existing" reasoning lets new
breakage stack on top of old. The 2026-07-05..07 window (~33h red, 4 independent
breakages, fixed by gastownhall/beads#4623 + #4624) and the 2026-07-07
CLI-docs-drift red (#4631) are both instances.

- **Check base health before merging anything.** `pr-preflight.sh` does this
  automatically since gastownhall/beads#4630 (per-workflow newest *decisive*
  run; cancelled runs are ignored, so a later green unrelated workflow cannot
  mask a red test workflow). Run the same check in blocking mode for the
  candidate PR:
  `PR_PREFLIGHT_BLOCK_RED_BASE=1 bd-main/scripts/pr-preflight.sh <pr-number> --repo gastownhall/beads`
- **While main is red, merge ONLY the fix for main.** Everything else waits,
  no matter how green its own checks look.
- **After the fix lands**, any PR whose green checks predate it must be
  refreshed (`gh pr update-branch`) and re-watched before judging.
- Autonomous agents run preflight with `PR_PREFLIGHT_BLOCK_RED_BASE=1` so a
  red base is a hard block rather than a warning (see AGENTS.md).

{"body":"## What

A step with both `needs = [X]` and `waits_for = "all-children"` (no explicit `from:`) used to crash `bd mol pour` with a dep-type collision. The `waits_for` spawner gets inferred from `needs[0]`, so both `needs` and `waits_for` emit edges on the same `(source, target)` pair — one as `DepBlocks`, one as `DepWaitsFor` — and storage rejects the duplicate. Pre-compute the `waits_for` spawner before processing `needs` and skip the redundant `DepBlocks` for that one target.

## Why

Fixes #3783.

The collision blocks the documented pattern where a step gates on the children of a step it depends on (the canonical "wait for the fanout from the surveyor" shape). Before this fix:

```
$ bd mol pour qnt-repro
Error: pouring proto: failed to create dependency:
  dependency qnt-mol-XXX -> qnt-mol-YYY already exists with type "blocks"
    (requested "waits-for"); remove it first with 'bd dep remove' then re-add
```

The `DepWaitsFor` edge already encodes the blocking semantics plus the gate metadata, so the `DepBlocks` edge from `needs` for that specific target is redundant once they collapse onto the same pair.

## Verification

```
go test -tags 'gms_pure_go cgo' -run TestBdMolPour_NeedsAndWaitsForSameTarget -v ./cmd/bd/
```

New e2e regression test at `cmd/bd/cook_qnt_test.go` pours a formula with the exact collision shape and asserts `bd mol pour` succeeds. Fails on `main` with the verbatim error; passes on this branch.

Sanity checks: cook test family (`TestSubstituteFormulaVars`, `TestSubstituteStepVarsRecursive`, `TestCompileTimeVsRuntimeMode`, `TestCreateGateIssue*`, `TestCookFormulaToSubgraph_*`) all pass. `go vet -tags 'gms_pure_go cgo' ./cmd/bd/` clean.

## Automated agent review — NEEDS-WORK (real crash fix, but a semantic gap)

> This is an automated agent review, not a maintainer approval. It is posted to help move the PR forward, per PR_MAINTAINER_GUIDELINES.

Thanks for chasing this — the crash is real and the de-dup mechanics are sound. There's one correctness gap worth resolving before merge.

### The bug is real (confirmed on main)
`collectDependencies` emits a `DepBlocks` edge for every `needs` entry (`cmd/bd/cook.go`), and a `waits_for` with no explicit `from:` infers its spawner from `needs[0]` and emits a `DepWaitsFor` edge on the **same** `(issue, spawner)` pair. Storage rejects a second edge of a different type on the same pair (`internal/storage/issueops/dependencies.go`), so `bd mol pour` hard-fails. Genuine bug.

### The concern: `waits_for` does not subsume `blocks` in the pre-fanout window
The fix drops the `blocks` edge on the premise that the `waits_for` edge already encodes the blocking. But the waits-for gate (`internal/storage/issueops/blocked_state.go`, `waitsForGateBlockedSQL`) blocks the waiter **only when the spawner has ≥1 open parent-child child** — it never blocks merely because the spawner itself is still open. At pour time (and until the spawner runs and fans out children), the spawner has zero children, so the gate evaluates to not-blocked. With the `blocks` edge removed, the waiter can become **ready before the spawner completes** — the opposite of what `needs` requested. On main the `blocks` edge kept it blocked until the spawner closed; the two edges are complementary.

### Two smaller points
- The skip is only in the `needs` loop; `depends_on` + an explicit matching `waits_for` would still collide (`cook.go` `depends_on` loop is untouched).
- `cmd/bd/cook_qnt_test.go` only asserts `mol pour` succeeds / no collision string — it never checks post-pour blocked state, so it wouldn't catch the premature-readiness regression.

### Suggested path
Make `waits_for` genuinely strictly-stronger than `blocks` so collapsing them is lossless: extend `waitsForGateBlockedSQL` to also block while the spawner itself is open (not just when it has open children), and add a test asserting the waiter stays blocked while the spawner is open with no children yet. Then dropping the `blocks` edge is safe. Happy to re-review once that's in.

You are working in the git worktree /var/home/matt/dev/mybd/.worktrees/beads/pr-3875-fixmerge (beads source, branch pr-3875-review = contributor jjgarzella's PR gastownhall/beads#3875, one commit c1904b9ef on an old base). Work ONLY in this worktree. Do NOT push anywhere — commit locally only.

Goal: make the PR merge-ready per the review feedback on the PR, preserving the contributor's commit.

Steps:

1. Rebase onto upstream/main: `git rebase upstream/main` (remote already fetched). Expect ~3 small conflict hunks in cmd/bd/cook.go and/or cmd/bd/cook_qnt_test.go; resolve them keeping both main's drift and the PR's logic (the PR pre-computes the waits_for spawner before the needs loop and skips emitting the DepBlocks edge for that one target).

2. Fix the semantic gap identified in review (this is the core work). The PR drops the `blocks` edge on the premise that the `waits-for` edge subsumes it, but `waitsForGateBlockedSQL` in internal/storage/issueops/blocked_state.go blocks the waiter ONLY while the spawner has ≥1 open parent-child child — it never blocks merely because the spawner itself is still open. So with the blocks edge dropped, the waiter can become ready BEFORE the spawner completes (pre-fanout window). Fix: extend `waitsForGateBlockedSQL` so the gate also blocks while the spawner itself is open. The spawner is referenced by `d.depends_on_issue_id` (issues table) or `d.depends_on_wisp_id` (wisps table). Concretely, wrap the existing first operand: change
   `( EXISTS(children-open in issues) OR EXISTS(children-open in wisps) )`
   to
   `( EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM issues sp WHERE sp.id = d.depends_on_issue_id AND sp.status <> 'closed' AND sp.status <> 'pinned') OR EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM wisps sp WHERE sp.id = d.depends_on_wisp_id AND sp.status <> 'closed' AND sp.status <> 'pinned') OR <existing two child EXISTS clauses> )`
   Keep the trailing `AND NOT (any-children ...)` clause unchanged. Note the any-children early-open semantics must be preserved: an 'any-children' gate with one closed child unblocks even if the spawner is still open — that is the existing documented behavior of any-children ("unblock as soon as any child closes"), so the NOT clause must still defeat the spawner-open operand. Verify the boolean structure delivers that: `(spawnerOpen OR childrenOpen) AND NOT (anyChildrenGate AND someChildClosed)` — yes, a closed child under any-children unblocks regardless. Add a brief SQL comment explaining the spawner-open clause (references the pre-fanout window).

3. Close the second review gap: in cmd/bd/cook.go `collectDependencies`, the dedup skip exists only in the `needs` loop; the `depends_on` loop can still emit a colliding DepBlocks against the same spawner target. Apply the same skip in the depends_on loop.

4. Tests (extend, don't replace, the contributor's cmd/bd/cook_qnt_test.go):
   a. Extend the existing pour test (or add a sibling) to assert post-pour blocked state: after pouring the needs+waits_for formula, the waiter issue must be BLOCKED while the spawner is open with zero children (this is the regression the review feared). Then close the spawner (no children ever spawned) and assert the waiter unblocks.
   b. Add a storage-level or e2e test for the gate itself if there is an existing test file for blocked_state / waits-for gates (search for existing tests referencing waitsForGate or waits-for blocked state, e.g. in internal/storage or cmd/bd) and extend it with: spawner open + no children → waiter blocked; spawner open + all-children gate + one open child → blocked; all children closed + spawner closed → unblocked; any-children gate + one closed child + spawner still open → UNBLOCKED (preserved early-open semantics).

   - `go vet -tags 'gms_pure_go cgo' ./cmd/bd/ ./internal/storage/...`
   - `CGO_ENABLED=1 go build -tags gms_pure_go ./cmd/bd` 
   - Run the touched test families: `CGO_ENABLED=1 go test -tags 'gms_pure_go cgo' -run 'TestBdMolPour_NeedsAndWaitsForSameTarget|<your new test names>' ./cmd/bd/ -v -timeout 600s` and whatever package holds the gate tests. Also run the pre-existing waits-for/blocked-state test families in the packages you touched to catch regressions.

6. Commit your changes as a SEPARATE commit on top of the contributor's (do not amend theirs). Commit message: `fix(storage): waits-for gate blocks while the spawner itself is open (GH#3783)` with a body explaining the pre-fanout window and noting it completes PR #3875 per review. Co-authored-by: jjgarzella <jjgarzella@users.noreply.github.com>

{"body":"Kills the ~10–20s/op connection churn against the hosted beads-gateway.

**Measured: ~37 ms/write saved (2.0×) at an 18 ms RTT** (latency-injected local bench; a lower bound — prod TLS makes each fresh dial costlier).

- **FIX #1** — `beginIgnoredTxOnBranch` borrows a warm connection from the main pool instead of a fresh single-conn `sql.DB` per write (MaxOpenConns==1 deadlock guard, InUse exhaustion pre-check, 250 ms bounded borrow; falls back to today's fresh-dial path when unsafe).
- **FIX #2** — `openSQLDB` builds a go-sql-driver `BeforeConnect` connector that re-resolves the cached credential token per new physical dial (hosted credential-command path only). Pooled connections survive EIA rotation. Local/static path byte-identical.
- **Follow-ups** — `resolveCredentialToken` honors the dial context; a MySQL 1045 invalidates the cached token so the retry re-mints.

Unit tests mutation-verified (deleting the BeforeConnect attachment / dropping the fallback credCmd fails the teeth tests); `go vet` clean; dolt-package tests pass in isolation (monolithic-run failures are docker-contention schema-init timeouts).

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)","comments":[{"a":"maphew","at":"2026-07-07T12:30:02Z","b":"Thanks Julian - this is a sharp fix for a real cost, and the workmanship shows. The BeforeConnect connector is the right tool for per-dial credential refresh - it is the driver's official extension point, keeps the token out of the DSN's hot path, and the fail-closed behavior on mint errors is exactly right. The test suite is genuinely good: the mock-driver teeth tests document what mutation each one catches, and the error paths assert the borrowed conn goes back to the pool (InUse==0).

Findings 3 (typed-1045-only auth classification) and 4 (side-pool token invalidation) remain open as normal-severity follow-ups - happy to fold them here if you want them in this PR, otherwise they can trail.

What still blocks the merge is only the stacking, and that call is y"}]}

Review gastownhall/beads PR #4316 ("Feature/4051" — minimum-viable file attachments for beads, `bd attachment add/list/copy/remove`, storing files under `.beads/attachments/<BEADID>/`). Read-only. Use `gh pr diff 4316 --repo gastownhall/beads` and `gh pr view 4316 --repo gastownhall/beads` for the code; the local beads source at /var/home/matt/dev/mybd/bd-main (branch upstream/main, already fetched) for current-main context. The PR is CONFLICTING with main and based on ~2026-06-07; note drift but review the design and code as submitted. Sibling PRs #4317 (Jira attachment sync) and #4318 (Linear attachment sync) stack on this — skim their descriptions only.

Purpose: this feeds a maintainer disposition + an owner scope decision. The charter (engdocs/PROJECT_CHARTER.md in the local repo) says: core owns issue-tracking primitives; schema is stable but changeable for pressing product need; beads syncs via Dolt (`refs/dolt/data` on the git remote) and should not become a storage engine; boundaries are fences, not bounce messages — prefer preserving value via simplification/metadata/integration routing.

Answer these, with file:line evidence:
1. **Sync semantics (suspected dominant flaw)**: attachments live as plain files under `.beads/attachments/`. Beads issue data syncs via the Dolt remote, NOT via git commits of .beads/. Do attachments sync at all in this design? What happens on a second clone / teammate machine — dangling attachment references? Does the PR address this (e.g. storing blobs in Dolt tables, or documenting local-only)? Check docs/ATTACHMENTS.md and docs/SYNC_SETUP.md changes in the diff.
2. **Schema/storage changes**: what does it add to internal/storage/dolt/ (attachments.go, counts.go, iter_stubs.go)? New tables? Does hash-identification actually dedupe/content-address, or is it filename-keyed?
3. **Code quality**: error handling, path traversal safety (attachment filenames → filesystem paths), Windows path handling, test coverage quality (attachment_test.go, attachment_embedded_test.go, attachment_policy_test.go — what do the policy tests enforce?).
4. **Charter fit options**: if the owner wants the capability but not this shape, what's the preserve-the-value routing? (e.g. metadata-only references to external URLs/paths; a plugin; Dolt-blob storage). Give a concrete recommendation ranked against the charter.
5. Anything genuinely broken (bugs, data loss, security) as opposed to design-debatable.

Return: a findings list (severity-tagged, file:line), a one-paragraph design verdict, and a recommended disposition from: Merge / Fix-merge / Redesign-reimplement / Reject / Owner-decision-required (with what exactly the owner must decide).

## What happened

Merged `upstream/main` into `pr-4581-fold`. All four predicted conflict files resolved, plus one unmarked incompatibility fixed mechanically (an `openLongTimeoutConn()` call site and several `applyResolvedConfig()` test call sites needed the `ctx` parameter that main's diff added but that these non-conflicting hunks hadn't been touched to match). `gofmt -l` is clean, `go vet` is clean, `CGO_ENABLED=1 go build -tags gms_pure_go ./cmd/bd` succeeds.

## Per-file conflict resolution

- **`internal/configfile/configfile.go`** (line ~422-468): HEAD added `TrustedDoltCredentialCommand()` (env var, then central config); main added `(*Config) GetDoltCredentialCommand()` (env var only). Both are called by different, independent code paths in the merged tree (`open.go`'s `resolveServerCredential` uses the trusted one; `gateway_credential.go`'s `ApplyGatewayCredential` uses the plain one). Kept both functions side by side rather than picking one.
- **`internal/storage/dolt/open.go`**: threaded main's new `ctx context.Context` param through `applyResolvedConfig`/its two callers (mechanical). For the credential-resolution block, composed main's `ApplyGatewayCredential(ctx, fileCfg, cfg)` gateway path (run only under `IsDoltServerMode()||IsSharedServerMode()`) followed unconditionally by our `resolveServerCredential(fileCfg, cfg)` fallback — this is the only resolution that preserves both hunks' literal content, since `resolveServerCredential` already no-ops once `cfg.ServerUser` is set. Kept our `resolveServerCredential` function definition (main's side of that hunk was empty — main deleted the equivalent code when it added its own).
- **`internal/storage/dolt/open_test.go`**: import list conflict was just "keep `fmt`" (used by later tests). Four other conflicts were all "add `ctx` arg" - resolved to the ctx form, then found and fixed 8 more identical non-conflicting call sites in the same file that needed the same signature update.
- **`internal/storage/dolt/store.go`**: metrics-struct/`init()` conflict was two independent new counters (`ignoredTxFreshPool` ours, `claimVerifyLost`/`claimVerifyRecovered` main's) — kept both. The ping/store-construction conflict merged main's `storeReady`/deferred-close pattern with our `retryStaleCredentialOpen` wrapper around the ping. The `DoltStore{}` literal conflict merged main's new `localActiveDatabaseDir` field with our `credCommand` field — both already exist on the struct definition, so this was additive.

## Nothing dropped

No PR code path was deleted outright — main's backend-simplification didn't remove anything the PR touched (sqlite/postgres/mysql direct backends were never part of PR #4581's diff).

## Real semantic incompatibility found — recommend stopping here

While chasing down the two remaining unmarked-but-broken call sites, I discovered upstream/main independently landed **a second, complete credential-command subsystem** for the same "hosted gateway connection" problem, via an earlier, separate PR ("choose your own storage backend", commits `3a9d9309d`/`28a8dc3b4`/`1fc38ba77`) that the backend-simplification refactor kept even after removing the sqlite/postgres/mysql backends themselves:

- `internal/creds/` package (own `resolveCredentialToken`, own `credRunner` package var, own cache) + `internal/storage/dolt/gateway_credential.go`'s `ApplyGatewayCredential` (identity-kind validation, `:@/`-char rejection, sets `cfg.Gateway`/`cfg.DisableAutoStart`) — main's mechanism.
- `internal/storage/dolt/credcmd.go` (own `resolveCredentialToken`, own `credRunner`) + `internal/storage/dolt/connector.go`'s `credentialBeforeConnect` (`sql/driver` `BeforeConnect` per-dial re-mint) — PR #4581's mechanism, which is what this task was scoped to fold in.

These are two independently-built, non-interacting implementations of the same idea (vendor-neutral credential-process helper, minted per dial). They don't call into each other and compile fine together, but two tests expose a real collision where I had to pick an ordering for the conflicted `applyResolvedConfig` credential block:

1. `TestApplyResolvedConfig_SetsCredentialCommand/trusted_env_credential_command_threaded_and_eager_token_seeded` (PR's own test) — **FAILS**. In server mode with `BEADS_DOLT_CREDENTIAL_COMMAND` set, main's `ApplyGatewayCredential` runs first (per its own precondition `IsDoltServerMode()||IsSharedServerMode()`), actually executes the shell command through `internal/creds`' own runner (not the `dolt` package's `credRunner` the test stubs), fails with `gasworks: command not found`, and aborts before our `resolveServerCredential`/per-dial connector ever engages. Even if the command succeeded, `ApplyGatewayCredential` sets `cfg.ServerUser` but never `cfg.CredentialCommand`, so PR #4581's whole point — per-dial token re-resolution via the `BeforeConnect` connector — would silently never activate for anyone using the gateway-server credential-command path, i.e. exactly PR #4581's target scenario.

2. `TestApplyResolvedConfigGatewayCredential/embedded_mode:_command_is_not_run_even_when_set` (main's own pre-existing regression test) — **FAILS** the other direction. It requires that in embedded mode a configured credential command never runs. `ApplyGatewayCredential` correctly gates on server mode, but our `resolveServerCredential` runs unconditionally after it — the PR's original assumption was "Dolt is always server-backed" (predating main's now-real embedded/server mode distinction), so it doesn't check mode at all and executes the helper anyway.

Fixing this correctly requires a maintainer/design decision, not a mechanical merge resolution — e.g., should the two credential subsystems be unified into one (single `credRunner`, single resolution/cache, single mode gate), should `ApplyGatewayCredential` be extended to also populate `cfg.CredentialCommand` so the per-dial connector covers the gateway path, and should `resolveServerCredential` be gated to the same `IsDoltServerMode()||IsSharedServerMode()` condition. I did not make that call.

- Worktree: `/var/home/matt/dev/mybd/.worktrees/beads/pr-4581-fold`, branch `pr-4581-fold`, mid-merge (`git status` shows "unmerged paths" — **not committed**, per instructions to stop rather than force).

- `go test ./internal/configfile/...` — all pass.
- `go test ./internal/storage/dolt/ -run 'TestIgnoredTx|TestOpenSQLDB|Credential|BeforeConnect'` — all pass except the two above (full log at `/tmp/claude-1000/-var-home-matt-dev-mybd/03353724-8668-472c-a128-448f9652b221/scratchpad/dolt-cred-tests.log`).

Files touched: `/var/home/matt/dev/mybd/.worktrees/beads/pr-4581-fold/internal/configfile/configfile.go`, `/var/home/matt/dev/mybd/.worktrees/beads/pr-4581-fold/internal/storage/dolt/open.go`, `/var/home/matt/dev/mybd/.worktrees/beads/pr-4581-fold/internal/storage/dolt/open_test.go`, `/var/home/matt/dev/mybd/.worktrees/beads/pr-4581-fold/internal/storage/dolt/store.go`.

Recommend the orchestrator/maintainer decide the reconciliation design before this merge is committed and PR #4581 proceeds — this is a genuine feature-overlap discovered by the merge, not a mechanical conflict.</result>

## Summary

Worktree: `/var/home/matt/dev/mybd/.worktrees/beads/pr-3875-fixmerge` (branch `pr-3875-review`), 2 commits ahead of `upstream/main` (`0c5fa422d`):
- `027d448fa` — contributor's rebased original commit (GH#3783 fix)
- `52ba524a1` — my new commit (depends_on-loop dedup fix only; see below)

### Step 1 — rebase (done, clean)

`git rebase upstream/main` produced exactly one conflict hunk in `cmd/bd/cook.go` (the pre-compute/dedup block auto-merged cleanly; only the final "emit the DepWaitsFor edge" block conflicted). Cause: main had since refactored that block to use a new `types.NewWaitsForDependency(issueID, spawnerIssueID, gate)` helper (constructing `Metadata` manually is gone), while the PR's old base still built `&types.Dependency{...Metadata: metaJSON}` by hand. Resolved by keeping main's `NewWaitsForDependency` helper call but wired to the PR's already-renamed `waitsForSpec`/`waitsForSpawnerStepID` variables. `cmd/bd/cook_qnt_test.go` (new file in the PR) applied with no conflict. Build/vet green after `rebase --continue`.

### Step 2 — the semantic gap (waitsForGateBlockedSQL): BLOCKED, reverted, not committed

I implemented exactly the SQL change specified (added `EXISTS(...sp.status<>'closed' AND sp.status<>'pinned'...)` clauses for the spawner itself, in `internal/storage/issueops/blocked_state.go`), plus a supporting fix in `AffectedByStatusChangeInTx`/`REDACTED` so a spawner's own close event triggers recompute for direct waiters (otherwise the SQL change would have no effect on close since the affected-ID seed set never included the waiter).

This **passed** my new regression test (spawner open + zero children → waiter blocked; spawner closes → waiter unblocks) but **broke** a pre-existing test:

```
=== NAME  TestIsBlocked_WaitsForDefaultGate
    is_blocked_test.go:284: expected waiter unblocked: all children closed under default gate
--- FAIL: TestIsBlocked_WaitsForDefaultGate (1.03s)
```

Root cause: `TestIsBlocked_WaitsForDefaultGate` (in `internal/storage/dolt/is_blocked_test.go`) never closes the spawner itself — only its one child — and asserts the waiter unblocks once "all children closed," documenting that the default (all-children) gate's readiness signal is fanout-completion (children done), independent of the spawner's own status. The task's specified boolean structure (`(spawnerOpen OR childrenOpen) AND NOT (anyChildrenGate AND someChildClosed)`) only carves out the any-children gate from the spawner-open block (verified: `TestIsBlocked_WaitsForAnyChildrenGate` still passed). It does **not** carve out all-children, so "spawner still open, all real children closed" now blocks under the literal spec — directly contradicting this pre-existing, documented test. This is the STOP condition the task anticipated; I did not force a resolution (e.g. by unilaterally deciding all-children should also require spawner-closed, or by inventing new gate semantics).

I reverted both `blocked_state.go` changes (SQL const and the `AffectedByStatusChange*` additions) back to upstream/main's exact code, and removed the demonstration test from `cmd/bd/cook_qnt_test.go` (it can't pass without the reverted change, so I didn't leave a permanently-failing test in the tree). `internal/storage/issueops/blocked_state.go` is now bit-identical to its rebased state (`git diff` shows no changes).

### Step 3 — depends_on-loop dedup gap: fixed, committed

Moved the `waitsForSpec`/`waitsForSpawnerStepID` pre-computation above both loops in `cmd/bd/cook.go::collectDependencies` and applied the same skip-if-matches-spawner check to the `depends_on` loop that already existed for `needs`. This is a small, independent, low-risk fix — it does not touch the disputed gate semantics. Committed as `52ba524a1`, with a message that documents exactly what landed and what didn't (see commit body above).

### Step 4 — tests

- 4a (pour + is_blocked assertion): written, confirmed the pre-fanout regression is real (failed without the disputed fix, passed with it) — but removed since it depends on the reverted fix.
- 4b (storage-level gate test): not added — same reason; extending `internal/storage/dolt/is_blocked_test.go` with a "spawner open, no children" case would just restate the disputed conflict already surfaced by the existing `TestIsBlocked_WaitsForDefaultGate`.

### Test results (full, final state)

```
CGO_ENABLED=1 go build -tags gms_pure_go ./...                     → clean
go vet -tags 'gms_pure_go cgo' ./cmd/bd/ ./internal/storage/...     → clean

go test -tags 'gms_pure_go cgo' ./internal/storage/dolt/ -run TestIsBlocked -v
  → PASS (all 16 subtests, including WaitsForDefaultGate, WaitsForAnyChildrenGate,
    AddClosedChildUnblocksAnyChildrenGate)

BEADS_TEST_EMBEDDED_DOLT=1 CGO_ENABLED=1 go test -tags 'gms_pure_go cgo' \
  -run 'TestBdMolPour_NeedsAndWaitsForSameTarget' ./cmd/bd/ -v
  → PASS

BEADS_TEST_EMBEDDED_DOLT=1 CGO_ENABLED=1 go test -tags 'gms_pure_go cgo' \
  -run 'TestBdMol|TestCook|TestPour|TestMol' ./cmd/bd/ -v
  → PASS (3 subtests SKIP: unrelated proxied-Dolt-server unavailability in this env)
```

### Concern for the orchestrator (design decision needed)

`waitsForGateBlockedSQL` genuinely cannot be extended to block on "spawner still open" without either (a) breaking the documented all-children semantics in `TestIsBlocked_WaitsForDefaultGate`, or (b) that test being wrong/outdated and needing a deliberate, reviewed change. Options I did not take unilaterally:
- Update `TestIsBlocked_WaitsForDefaultGate` itself to require the spawner closed too (changes documented default-gate behavior for every existing waits-for user, not just this PR's dropped-blocks-edge case — blast radius unclear).
- Scope the spawner-open block to only fire when the DepWaitsFor edge's paired DepBlocks edge was actually dropped by this PR's dedup (i.e., track that provenance somehow) rather than changing the gate's general semantics — no such signal exists in the dependency row today.
- Leave PR gastownhall/beads#3875 landing without closing this gap, i.e. document the residual pre-fanout-window risk in the PR itself and let a human/maintainer decide.

- `/var/home/matt/dev/mybd/.worktrees/beads/pr-3875-fixmerge/cmd/bd/cook.go` (committed, `52ba524a1`)
- `/var/home/matt/dev/mybd/.worktrees/beads/pr-3875-fixmerge/cmd/bd/cook_qnt_test.go` (rebase-merged only, contributor's original, unmodified from rebase result)
- `/var/home/matt/dev/mybd/.worktrees/beads/pr-3875-fixmerge/internal/storage/issueops/blocked_state.go` (attempted, then reverted — no net change vs. upstream/main)

Working tree is clean; nothing pushed anywhere per instructions.</result>

input.summary: Refined fix: also_blocks metadata-scoped spawner gate
input.message:
Excellent stop — the TestIsBlocked_WaitsForDefaultGate conflict was exactly the right thing to surface. Here is the design decision: we take a provenance-scoped fix instead of changing general gate semantics. Implement this in the same worktree, on top of your commit 52ba524a1:

1. In cmd/bd/cook.go collectDependencies: at the two places (needs loop + depends_on loop) where you skip emitting the DepBlocks edge because it collapses into the waits-for edge, arrange for the waits-for edge to carry an extra metadata key `also_blocks: true` alongside the existing `gate` key. Main's helper types.NewWaitsForDependency builds the metadata; either add a variant/option (e.g. NewWaitsForBlockingDependency or a bool arg — pick the least invasive form consistent with the types package style) or set/patch the Metadata JSON after construction. Only collapsed edges get the flag; a plain waits_for with no matching needs/depends_on must NOT get it.

2. In internal/storage/issueops/blocked_state.go: re-apply your spawner-open clauses, but scoped and positioned differently — append to the very end of the existing waitsForGateBlockedSQL expression, OUTSIDE the existing AND NOT(any-children) carve-out:
   `OR ( COALESCE(JSON_UNQUOTE(JSON_EXTRACT(d.metadata, '$.also_blocks')), 'false') = 'true' AND ( EXISTS(spawner issue open) OR EXISTS(spawner wisp open) ) )`
   using your previous spawner-open EXISTS subqueries (sp.status <> 'closed' AND sp.status <> 'pinned'). Rationale in a SQL comment: a collapsed needs+waits_for edge carries blocks semantics too, so it additionally blocks while the spawner itself is open — and this must override the any-children early-open carve-out (needs means the spawner itself must close), hence the OR at top level. Legacy rows lack the key → COALESCE 'false' → zero behavior change for existing edges.

3. Re-apply your AffectedByStatusChangeInTx / REDACTED additions so a spawner's own close triggers recompute of direct waiters (needed for the new clause to take effect on close).

4. Restore your regression tests, adapted to the flag:
   - pour-level (cmd/bd/cook_qnt_test.go): pour needs+waits_for formula → waiter BLOCKED while spawner open with zero children; close spawner → waiter unblocks.
   - storage-level (internal/storage/dolt/is_blocked_test.go): new subtest for an also_blocks waits-for edge: spawner open + no children → blocked; any-children gate + one closed child + spawner still open → STILL BLOCKED (the override); spawner closed + gate satisfied → unblocked. And verify the existing TestIsBlocked_WaitsForDefaultGate and TestIsBlocked_WaitsForAnyChildrenGate still pass unmodified.
   - Check whether dependencies-table JSON metadata round-trips through any export/import (bd dep list --json etc.) that asserts exact metadata shape; if a test breaks on the new key, adjust expectations.

5. Validate as before (build, vet, TestIsBlocked family, TestBdMolPour family, TestBdMol/TestCook sweep). 

6. Commit as one commit on top: `fix(storage): collapsed needs+waits_for edges also block while the spawner is open (GH#3783)` — body explaining the also_blocks provenance flag, why general gate semantics are unchanged, and the any-children override rationale. Trailer:
Agent-Signature: claude-code-sonnet-builder on behalf of maphew

Do not push. Report diff summary + full test results. If Dolt's JSON_EXTRACT/JSON_UNQUOTE behaves differently than expected for boolean true (e.g. JSON true unquotes to 'true' vs '1'), test both storage paths and adjust the predicate accordingly — note what you found.

<note>A task-notification fires each time this agent stops with no live background children of its own. The user can send it another message and resume it, so the same task-id may notify more than once.</note>
<result>## Findings

### Blockers

**B1. `bd attachment prune` permanently destroys the only copy of bytes, driven by a branch-scoped index.** `cmd/bd/attachment.go:328-352` (prune) + `cmd/bd/attachment.go:445-471` (`referencedAttachmentPaths`). Reachability is computed from the *current Dolt branch's working set* (`SearchIssues` + `ListAttachments`), but the bytes it deletes live outside Dolt and are, per the PR's own doc, not covered by `bd dolt push` or `bd backup`. So:

- `bd branch feat` → attach → `bd checkout main` → `bd attachment prune` deletes the bytes; switching back leaves a permanently dangling row. `bd branch` is real (`cmd/bd/branch.go:11`), so this is not hypothetical.
- Any pull/merge/revert that transiently drops an attachment row makes its bytes prune-eligible; re-merging restores the row but not the file.
- No confirmation prompt, no `--force`, no trash/quarantine. `--dry-run` exists but is opt-in.

Fix: at minimum require an explicit confirmation and compute reachability across all local branches (`dolt_branches` / `AS OF`), or move deletions to a quarantine dir with a grace period. A GC that deletes unversioned data using a versioned index is unsound as written.

**B2. Migration number collides with main.** `internal/storage/schema/migrations/0050_create_attachments.up.sql` — main already ships `0050_dependencies_deterministic_id.*` and is at `0059`. Mechanical, but it will silently mis-order or trip the migration-hash machinery (`internal/storage/schema/migration_content_hashes.go`) if merged as-is. Renumber to the next free slot.

**B3. ~660 added lines target a directory that no longer exists.** All `website/**` hunks (diff lines 2760-3939), including `website/versioned_docs/version-1.0.0|1.0.4|1.0.5/...`. Upstream deleted the Docusaurus site in `52aea3f7e` ("go all-in on Mintlify"). Separately, `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`, `docs/SYNC_SETUP.md`, `docs/DOC_INVENTORY.md`, `docs/UNINSTALLING.md` no longer exist at those paths (internal docs moved to `engdocs/` in `0e017821f`). Also: retroactively editing `versioned_docs/version-1.0.0` to document a command that did not exist in 1.0.0 was wrong even before the deletion. This is most of the CONFLICTING state.

### Should-fix

**S1. Attachments are invisible to wisps, and fail with a misleading error.** `internal/storage/issueops/attachments.go:24-30` checks `SELECT EXISTS(... FROM issues WHERE id = ?)` and the FK targets `issues(id)` only. Comments handle this correctly with table routing — `internal/storage/issueops/comments.go:20-22` routes to `wisp_comments` via `IsActiveWispInTx`. So `bd attachment add <wisp-id>` resolves the issue fine at `cmd/bd/attachment.go:52-84` and then dies with `issue X: not found` *after* the bytes have already been written to disk (and are not cleaned up on this path, since `attachmentRelPathReferenced` returns `false` → the file *is* removed; fine — but the error text is wrong). Either add wisp routing or reject wisps explicitly with a clear message.

**S2. `bd show` JSON now always materializes the full attachment list, breaking the count-only contract.** `cmd/bd/show.go:159-161`. The surrounding block is explicitly documented (`cmd/bd/show.go:145-146`, "be-ijck6q: default is count-only ... Use `--include-dependents` / `--include-comments` to stream the full lists"), and dependents/comments are gated behind flags at `cmd/bd/show.go:161` and `:208`. `details.Attachments` is set unconditionally. Add `--include-attachments` and gate it (that is also the only thing `IterAttachments` would be for — see S3).

**S3. Four of the six new `Storage` interface methods are dead weight.** `internal/storage/storage.go:+131` adds `IterAttachments`; it has zero production callers (implemented in `dolt`, `embeddeddolt`, `telemetry`, and the Jira test fake — nothing calls it). `ResolveAttachment` and `CountAttachments` could equally be helpers over `ListAttachments`. Each interface method costs every fake in the tree — `internal/jira/tracker_test.go:+708-716,+758,+777` already shows the ripple. Against the charter's "widen the interface [only] if the current storage interface cannot express a needed operation", the minimal surface is `AddAttachment` / `ListAttachments` / `RemoveAttachment`.

**S4. `bd show` queries attachments twice per issue.** `cmd/bd/show.go:159-161` (JSON path) and `cmd/bd/show.go:276` (text path) both call `ListAttachments`; the text path adds an unconditional extra round-trip to every `bd show`, including the common no-attachments case where `CountAttachments` would do.

**S5. `prune`/`fsck` are O(issues) round-trips.** `cmd/bd/attachment.go:445-471` iterates every issue and issues one `ListAttachments` query each. `SELECT DISTINCT storage_relpath FROM attachments` is one query. On a 10k-issue tracker this is 10k queries plus full issue hydration (`SearchIssues` with the wide projection).

**S6. Unescaped `LIKE` metacharacters in a destructive selector.** `internal/storage/issueops/attachments.go:89`: `content_hash LIKE ?` with `selector+"%"`. `bd attachment remove <id> '%'` matches every attachment on the issue; with exactly one attachment it silently resolves and deletes it. Escape `%`/`_`, or only take the hash-prefix branch when the selector is `^[0-9a-f]+$`.

**S7. Duplicate content on one issue surfaces a raw SQL error.** `UNIQUE KEY uniq_attachments_issue_hash (issue_id, hash_algorithm, content_hash)` in the migration means attaching identical bytes under a second filename fails with a bare `Error 1062` through `FatalErrorRespectJSON("adding attachment metadata: %v", ...)` at `cmd/bd/attachment.go:96-102`. No data loss (the cleanup guard correctly keeps the shared file), but map it to "already attached as `<name>`".

**S8. Policy tests assert exact doc prose.** `cmd/bd/attachment_policy_test.go:9-30` fails the build on ten literal substrings of `docs/ATTACHMENTS.md`, including markdown backticks and the sentence fragment `` "`bd show` and `bd attachment list` report those entries as" ``. Given B3 (docs tree moved), this test is already broken; more generally, prose-coupled build gates are a maintenance tax the docs-drift scripts (`scripts/check-cli-docs-drift.sh`) already partly cover. cmd/bd/cook.go                             |  70 ++++++++---
 cmd/bd/cook_qnt_test.go                    | 185 +++++++++++++++++++++++++++++
 cmd/bd/template.go                         |   6 +
 internal/storage/dolt/is_blocked_test.go   | 100 ++++++++++++++++
 internal/storage/issueops/blocked_state.go |  93 +++++++++++----
 internal/types/types.go                    |  36 ++++++
 6 files changed, 450 insertions(+), 40 deletions(-)
commit 53e8fd31a8ec3fd8324f0a9f186249305f73b7ee
Author: matt wilkie <maphew@gmail.com>
Date:   Sun Jul 26 11:15:39 2026 -0700

    fix(storage): collapsed needs+waits_for edges also block while the spawner is open (GH#3783)
    
    Design decision (superseding the reverted general-gate attempt in
    52ba524a1): instead of changing waitsForGateBlockedSQL's semantics for
    every waits-for edge, scope the spawner-open block to edges that
    provably collapsed a redundant DepBlocks edge into their DepWaitsFor
    edge.
    
    - types.WaitsForMeta gains also_blocks (bool, omitempty). A new
      types.NewWaitsForBlockingDependency wraps NewWaitsForDependency and
      sets it; NewWaitsForDependency and every other existing caller are
      unchanged, so plain waits-for edges keep exactly their prior
      metadata shape.
    - cmd/bd/cook.go collectDependencies now tracks whether it actually
      skipped a depends_on/needs entry because it matched the waits_for
      spawner (waitsForCollapsedBlocks); only then does it call
      NewWaitsForBlockingDependency instead of NewWaitsForDependency. A
      plain waits_for with no matching needs/depends_on entry never gets
      the flag.
    - waitsForGateBlockedSQL gets one more top-level OR clause: when
      also_blocks is 'true' (COALESCEd to 'false' for legacy/plain rows,
      so this is a no-op for them), the gate also blocks while the spawner
      issue/wisp itself is open. It is a top-level OR specifically so it
      overrides the any-children early-open carve-out: a collapsed edge
      means the original needs/depends_on required the spawner itself to
      close, so an early child-close under any-children must not unblock
      the waiter while the spawner remains open. Confirmed by
      TestIsBlocked_WaitsForAlsoBlocksOverridesAnyChildrenEarlyOpen.
    - AffectedByStatusChangeInTx / REDACTED now
      also seed direct waiters on the closing/reopening id as spawner
      (loadWaitersOnSpawnerIDsInTx), so a spawner's own status change
      triggers is_blocked recompute for a waiter connected only by a
      DepWaitsFor edge (no DepBlocks edge to hang the old propagation
      off of).
    - cmd/bd/template.go cloneSubgraph: found while debugging the new
      pour-level regression test — cloning a template's dependencies into
      a poured mol never copied dep.Metadata, so every poured waits-for
      edge silently reset to an empty/default gate with also_blocks unset
      regardless of what collectDependencies produced. Now copies
      Metadata through.
    
    Existing TestIsBlocked_WaitsForDefaultGate and
    TestIsBlocked_WaitsForAnyChildrenGate pass unmodified: general
    waits-for gate semantics are untouched for every edge without
    also_blocks.
    
    New coverage: TestIsBlocked_WaitsForAlsoBlocksSpawnerOpen,
    TestIsBlocked_WaitsForAlsoBlocksOverridesAnyChildrenEarlyOpen
    (internal/storage/dolt/is_blocked_test.go), and
    TestBdMolPour_NeedsAndWaitsForSameTarget_SpawnerOpenBlocksWaiter
    (cmd/bd/cook_qnt_test.go, exercises the embedded-Dolt/GMS pour path
    end to end).
    
    JSON_UNQUOTE(JSON_EXTRACT(...)) on a JSON boolean true unquotes to the
    string "true" (not "1") consistently on both the dolt-sql-server path
    (internal/storage/dolt tests) and the embedded pure-Go GMS path
    (internal/storage/embeddeddolt, probed directly) — the COALESCE(...,
    'false') = 'true' predicate needed no engine-specific variant.
    
    Agent-Signature: claude-fable-5-medium on behalf of matt wilkie

--- a/internal/storage/issueops/blocked_state.go

@@ -21,40 +21,73 @@ type DBTX interface {
 
 const waitsForGateBlockedSQL = `
 		(
-		  EXISTS (
-		    SELECT 1 FROM dependencies cd JOIN issues child ON child.id = cd.issue_id
-		    WHERE cd.type = 'parent-child'
-		      AND ((d.depends_on_issue_id IS NOT NULL AND cd.depends_on_issue_id = d.depends_on_issue_id)
-		        OR (d.depends_on_wisp_id IS NOT NULL AND cd.depends_on_wisp_id = d.depends_on_wisp_id))
-		      AND child.status <> 'closed' AND child.status <> 'pinned'
-		  )

-		    WHERE cd.type = 'parent-child'
-		      AND ((d.depends_on_issue_id IS NOT NULL AND cd.depends_on_issue_id = d.depends_on_issue_id)
-		        OR (d.depends_on_wisp_id IS NOT NULL AND cd.depends_on_wisp_id = d.depends_on_wisp_id))

    fix(storage): collapsed needs+waits_for edges also block while the spawner is open (GH#3783)

    52ba524a1): instead of changing waitsForGateBlockedSQL's semantics for
    every waits-for edge, scope the spawner-open block to edges that
    provably collapsed a redundant DepBlocks edge into their DepWaitsFor
    edge.
    
    - types.WaitsForMeta gains also_blocks (bool, omitempty). A new
      types.NewWaitsForBlockingDependency wraps NewWaitsForDependency and
      sets it; NewWaitsForDependency and every other existing caller are
      unchanged, so plain waits-for edges keep exactly their prior
      metadata shape.
    - cmd/bd/cook.go collectDependencies now tracks whether it actually
      skipped a depends_on/needs entry because it matched the waits_for
      spawner (waitsForCollapsedBlocks); only then does it call
      NewWaitsForBlockingDependency instead of NewWaitsForDependency. A
      plain waits_for with no matching needs/depends_on entry never gets
      the flag.
    - waitsForGateBlockedSQL gets one more top-level OR clause: when
      also_blocks is 'true' (COALESCEd to 'false' for legacy/plain rows,
      so this is a no-op for them), the gate also blocks while the spawner
      issue/wisp itself is open. It is a top-level OR specifically so it
      overrides the any-children early-open carve-out: a collapsed edge
      means the original needs/depends_on required the spawner itself to
      close, so an early child-close under any-children must not unblock
      the waiter while the spawner remains open. Confirmed by
      TestIsBlocked_WaitsForAlsoBlocksOverridesAnyChildrenEarlyOpen.
    - AffectedByStatusChangeInTx / REDACTED now
      also seed direct waiters on the closing/reopening id as spawner
      (loadWaitersOnSpawnerIDsInTx), so a spawner's own status change
      triggers is_blocked recompute for a waiter connected only by a
      DepWaitsFor edge (no DepBlocks edge to hang the old propagation
      off of).
    - cmd/bd/template.go cloneSubgraph: found while debugging the new
      pour-level regression test — cloning a template's dependencies into
      a poured mol never copied dep.Metadata, so every poured waits-for
      edge silently reset to an empty/default gate with also_blocks unset
      regardless of what collectDependencies produced. Now copies
      Metadata through.
